status: IMPLEMENTATION INVENTORY — proposed classifications require publisher review before submission
warning: This worksheet is not a privacy policy, a completed store disclosure, or a claim that data is not collected.

candidate_data_inventory.data: Verified phone number and account identifier
candidate_data_inventory.planned_purpose: Account creation, authentication, and contact identity
candidate_data_inventory.actual_processing: Verified phone number and Firebase UID; app stores normalized E.164 number and account timestamps.
candidate_data_inventory.providers: Google Firebase Authentication; Google Cloud Firestore
candidate_data_inventory.stored_where: Firebase Authentication and private Firestore user record
candidate_data_inventory.retention: Until account deletion; Google may keep abuse-prevention records under its policy.
candidate_data_inventory.deletion: Durable server deletion disables the Auth user, removes account data, then removes Auth user.
candidate_data_inventory.store_classification: Proposed: phone number, user ID; linked to user; app functionality/security.

candidate_data_inventory.data: Device address-book entries or discovery inputs
candidate_data_inventory.actual_processing: Only a contact explicitly selected in the native picker is copied into the add-person form. No bulk address-book upload.
candidate_data_inventory.providers: Device contact picker; selected saved fields then Google Cloud Firestore
candidate_data_inventory.stored_where: Device before save; private user contacts after save
candidate_data_inventory.retention: Until replaced by saving the same number, or account deletion.
candidate_data_inventory.deletion: Removed with the account; another person’s own address book remains under their control.
candidate_data_inventory.store_classification: Proposed: contacts; optional, linked to user; app functionality.

candidate_data_inventory.actual_processing: Entered name and normalized phone number are saved; blocked numbers are stored privately.
candidate_data_inventory.retention: Contacts until replaced or account deletion; blocking until unblocked or account deletion.
candidate_data_inventory.deletion: Recursive account deletion includes saved contacts and blocking data.
candidate_data_inventory.store_classification: Proposed: contacts / other user content; optional, linked to user; app functionality.

candidate_data_inventory.actual_processing: Native WebRTC transports live voice with encrypted media. No app/server recording feature is implemented.
candidate_data_inventory.providers: Peer phone; Cloudflare TURN when relayed
candidate_data_inventory.stored_where: Transient media buffers; no FamCall audio archive
candidate_data_inventory.deletion: Transient buffers close with the call.
candidate_data_inventory.store_classification: Review ephemeral-processing exceptions separately for Apple and Google; do not mark audio as recorded.

candidate_data_inventory.data: Call signaling, participants, timing and call state
candidate_data_inventory.actual_processing: Call documents include participant UIDs/numbers, times and outcome. SDP/ICE can expose connection addresses to the peer and signaling backend.
candidate_data_inventory.stored_where: Shared call document with participant-only rules; signaling subcollections
candidate_data_inventory.retention: History 90 days; signaling deleted after terminal state with retryable trigger.
candidate_data_inventory.deletion: Account deletion removes associated call documents and subcollections.
candidate_data_inventory.store_classification: Proposed: product interaction / other usage data and identifiers; linked to user; app functionality.

candidate_data_inventory.data: Notification tokens and device/app integrity signals
candidate_data_inventory.actual_processing: Installation identifier, OS push token and token type registered for ringing. App Attest/Play Integrity validate genuine apps.
candidate_data_inventory.providers: Apple APNs/App Attest/DeviceCheck; Google FCM/App Check
candidate_data_inventory.stored_where: Private Firestore device registration; provider verification systems
candidate_data_inventory.retention: Device registrations expire after 60 days without renewal; provider retention must be reviewed.
candidate_data_inventory.deletion: Device records removed on account deletion.
candidate_data_inventory.store_classification: Proposed: device identifiers; linked to user; app functionality/security.

candidate_data_inventory.data: IP addresses, network telemetry and service logs
candidate_data_inventory.actual_processing: Providers receive ordinary network information. Production app sends no lab RTC diagnostics. Per-user abuse counters protect calls/contacts/relay issuance.
candidate_data_inventory.providers: Google Cloud/Firebase; Cloudflare; Apple for push
candidate_data_inventory.stored_where: Cloud service logs and private rate-limit counters
candidate_data_inventory.retention: Counters 2 days; operational logs target 30 days; provider-required security/audit records may differ.
candidate_data_inventory.deletion: Counters/logs expire by configured retention; verify deployed settings.
candidate_data_inventory.store_classification: Review diagnostics and IP-derived location classification with each provider’s current policy.

candidate_data_inventory.data: Crash reports or analytics, if selected
candidate_data_inventory.actual_processing: No Firebase Analytics, Crashlytics or advertising SDK selected. No app analytics endpoint in production.
candidate_data_inventory.store_classification: Proposed: no advertising tracking; recheck final binary and SDK manifests.

candidate_data_inventory.data: Support correspondence and voluntary test feedback
candidate_data_inventory.actual_processing: Support emails are received only when the person chooses to contact support.
candidate_data_inventory.retention: Owner must set and operate the support retention policy.
candidate_data_inventory.deletion: Handled by support after proportionate ownership verification.
candidate_data_inventory.store_classification: Proposed: email address and support content, optional, linked where provided; customer support.

questions_for_each_data_item: Does it leave the device, and can a provider access it beyond servicing the request in real time?
Is it required or optional? What permission or consent is used?
Is it linked to a person, account, device, or another identifier?
Is it collected, shared, or subject to a store-defined exception? Use each store's definitions separately.
Is it used for tracking or advertising? Do any SDK defaults introduce those purposes?
What is protected in transit and at rest, and what is the actual media encryption model?
Who receives it, where is it stored, how long is it kept, and what happens on deletion?

must_resolve.terms_or_license_choice: MIT source license; service terms draft at /terms
must_resolve.in_app_deletion_path: Settings → Delete account → recent phone verification → confirm
must_resolve.deletion_verification_process: Recent Firebase phone auth in app; ownership verification by support for external requests
must_resolve.deletion_completion_window: Asynchronous server retries; external support response time requires publisher policy
must_resolve.retained_data_and_reason: Completion marker 30 days for retry safety; provider security/legal records per provider policy
must_resolve.retention_periods: See implemented inventory and production retention verification gate
must_resolve.ads_declaration: No ads implemented; publisher to confirm final submission
must_resolve.required_sdk_privacy_manifests: Inspect final archived build; simulator build alone is insufficient

deletion_acceptance_checks: A signed-in user can find and initiate account deletion in the app.
A person without the app installed can find and initiate a deletion request on the external web resource.
The process verifies identity without relying on an inaccessible account or excessive steps.
Deletion affects the defined account and associated data; it is not only deactivation.
Any retained data, legitimate reason, and time limit match the policy and actual implementation.
Active sessions, call permissions, notifications and contact discovery stop behaving as if the deleted account remains active.
